question: A 4-month-old boy with a history of multiple infections presents with muscle stiffness. On physical exam, he is found to have carpopedal spasm as well as a heart murmur. Based on your clinical suspicion you decide to obtain a chest X-ray which shows a diminished shadow in the mediastinum. A mutation in which of the following chromosomes is the most likely cause of this patient's presentation?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "4-month-old boy" -> "history of multiple infections" -> "possible immunodeficiency" -> "muscle stiffness and carpopedal spasm" -> "possible hypocalcemia" -> "heart murmur suggests cardiac involvement" -> "diminished mediastinal shadow on chest X-ray" -> "possible thymic hypoplasia" -> "associated with DiGeorge syndrome" -> "DiGeorge syndrome linked to chromosome 22" -> 85%

CHAIN: "4-month-old boy" -> "multiple infections" -> "suggests underlying condition" -> "muscle stiffness and carpopedal spasm" -> "indicates possible electrolyte imbalance" -> "heart murmur indicates cardiac issues" -> "diminished mediastinal shadow" -> "could indicate thymic absence" -> "thymic absence associated with DiGeorge syndrome" -> "DiGeorge syndrome linked to chromosome 22" -> 90%

CHAIN: "4-month-old boy" -> "history of infections" -> "suggests immunological disorder" -> "muscle stiffness and carpopedal spasm" -> "indicates possible metabolic or electrolyte issue" -> "heart murmur present" -> "diminished mediastinal shadow on X-ray" -> "suggests thymic hypoplasia" -> "thymic hypoplasia associated with chromosome 22 abnormalities" -> 80%

CHAIN: "4-month-old boy" -> "multiple infections" -> "possible genetic disorder" -> "muscle stiffness and carpopedal spasm" -> "indicates possible calcium or magnesium issue" -> "heart murmur present" -> "diminished mediastinal shadow" -> "could indicate thymic issues" -> "thymic issues often linked to chromosome 22" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation of this 4-month-old boy, including muscle stiffness, carpopedal spasm, heart murmur, and diminished mediastinal shadow, suggests a diagnosis of DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion syndrome). This condition is associated with immunodeficiency (leading to multiple infections), hypoparathyroidism (causing muscle stiffness and spasms), and congenital heart defects (indicated by the heart murmur). The mutation associated with DiGeorge syndrome is located on chromosome 22.
